rationale: Iteration 4 (kp 7.0, kd 0.5, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction) is the best raced design so far at 94.32, but every trial still ran off track. Raising kd from 0.4 to 0.5 did not bring oval steering_oscillation below 0.2. It rose slightly from 0.250 to 0.267, so the damping step did not work on its own. The plan agreed with the Evaluator covers this case: if oscillation stays above 0.2 with kd 0.5, raise kd to 0.6 before lowering kp. Lowering kp now would weaken the edge response that keeps max_error near 0.064, which is still just over the 0.06 limit. Other evidence: s-bend oscillation is 0.16 and slalom is 0.12, both low. Line losses are 1.6 on the oval, 1.35 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom. Progress is 0.46 on the oval, 0.15 on the s-bend and 0.09 on the slalom. Body width cannot relax the off-track limit, so control has to fix it. Change: kd 0.5 to 0.6, with kp 7.0, geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction unchanged, so the result isolates damping. Expected result: oval steering_oscillation falls to about 0.2 or below, max_error holds at or below about 0.063, and oval progress holds or improves. Risk: kd 0.6 amplifies sensor noise and may slow the response at bend entries, which could raise max_error on the s-bend. Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation, max_error and line_loss_events per track, plus progress, rms_error and control_effort. Next steps depend on the result. If oscillation is now low and max_error is still at or above 0.06, widen the array to ±0.040 m and test kp near 8. If oscillation stays above 0.2 at kd 0.6, reduce kp slightly toward 6.5. If line losses remain at the same bend entries, test line_loss search_left or search_right, favouring the side the failing bends turn towards. If progress is still below 1 with max_error under 0.06, raise base_speed toward 1.6.
